_comment: A worked manifest — the half of a model's surface that no repository scan can see.
Copy this file, change the agent block, replace the capabilities with your own, then:
Record environment variable NAMES only. Never a value. This repository is public.
Keys beginning with _ are ignored by the loader.

agent.name: Claude Code
agent.note: The agent that built bin/ and maintains wiki/. Runs locally and as a remote web session.

capabilities.name: claude-code
capabilities.title: Claude Code
capabilities.summary: Anthropic's coding agent: shell, file read/write, edit, glob, grep, task delegation, scheduled triggers and artifact publishing. Runs as a terminal CLI, a desktop app, an IDE extension and a remote web session against a cloned repo.
capabilities.instructions: Governing entrypoint is CLAUDE.md at the repository root. Session order is fixed: read LLM_HANDOFF.md and operator-log.md, run bin/wiki-work, do the operator's request in full, then drain obligations from the top. Gate with bin/wiki-check before every commit.

capabilities.name: github
capabilities.title: GitHub MCP server
capabilities.summary: The only GitHub access a remote Claude Code session has — there is no gh CLI and no direct API. Pull requests, issues, reviews, checks, file contents, branches, commits, code search. Tools are prefixed mcp__github__.
capabilities.instructions: In a remote session `gh` and `hub` are absent and unauthenticated curl to github.com returns 404 for private repos even when the session is authorised. Use these tools rather than concluding a repository is unreachable. Repository scope is fixed at session start; add_repo widens it.

capabilities.name: claude-code-remote
capabilities.title: Claude Code Remote
capabilities.summary: Session and schedule control for remote runs: attach repositories, spawn and message sibling sessions, list environments, and create Routines (cron triggers) that fire a prompt into this session or a fresh one.
capabilities.instructions: send_later schedules a message back into this session and survives container restarts — it is the correct way to re-check a PR rather than polling with sleep. create_trigger cron expressions are evaluated in UTC.

capabilities.name: Explore
capabilities.summary: Read-only fan-out search agent for sweeping many files or naming conventions at once. Reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code but does not audit it.
capabilities.instructions: Specify search breadth explicitly — 'medium' or 'very thorough'. Do not use where a single Grep would answer; the cold start costs more than the search.

capabilities.name: general-purpose
capabilities.summary: Full-tool agent for multi-step research and execution where the parent only needs the conclusion.
capabilities.instructions: Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context the parent already has. In this repository, prefer working inline: a wiki pass depends on CLAUDE.md, the specs and the handoff, none of which a fresh agent carries.

capabilities.name: skill-creator
capabilities.summary: Create, edit and evaluate skills; measure trigger accuracy and benchmark a skill's description against variance analysis.
capabilities.instructions: Relevant here when writing anything under skills/ or .claude/skills/ — it is the tooling half of skills/PROTOCOL.md's promotion step.

capabilities.name: code-review
capabilities.summary: Review a diff, PR, branch or path for correctness bugs and simplification at a chosen effort level; --comment posts findings inline on a PR, --fix applies them.

capabilities.name: docx
capabilities.summary: Read, create and edit Word documents and templates, including tracked changes and comments.

capabilities.name: xlsx
capabilities.summary: Read, create and repair spreadsheets and delimited files — formulas, formatting, charts, and restructuring messy tabular data.
capabilities.instructions: Relevant to this repository's message exports: the per-contact CSVs contain embedded newlines inside quoted message text, so line counts are not record counts. Parse, never wc -l.

capabilities.name: pdf
capabilities.summary: Extract text and tables from PDFs, merge, split, fill forms, and OCR scanned documents.

capabilities.name: pptx
capabilities.summary: Create, read and edit PowerPoint presentations, layouts, templates and speaker notes.

capabilities.name: dataviz
capabilities.summary: Chart and dashboard design method — form heuristics, an accessible colour formula with a runnable validator, mark specs and interaction rules. Read before writing any chart code in any medium.
capabilities.instructions: Constrained here by THE RULE in caakehorn/home: a visual channel must encode a count, a date or a length — never a score, a mood, or a category somebody chose.

capabilities.name: artifact-design
capabilities.summary: Design calibration for published Artifact pages — load before writing one, including a Markdown one.

capabilities.name: security-review
capabilities.summary: Security review of the pending changes on the current branch.
capabilities.instructions: Worth running against anything that touches skills/registry/ or intake/: both write to a public repository from a browser.

capabilities.name: update-config
capabilities.summary: Configure the harness through settings.json — permissions, environment variables, and hooks. Automated 'whenever X happens' behaviour must be a hook; the harness runs those, not the model.

capabilities.name: session-start-hook
capabilities.summary: Set up a repository for Claude Code on the web — a SessionStart hook that installs dependencies so tests and linters can run in a fresh remote container.

capabilities.name: Artifact
capabilities.summary: Publish an HTML page to a private, shareable URL on claude.ai, with optional runtime capabilities. Useful for handing the operator a rendered view of corpus data without deploying to the portal.

capabilities.name: WebSearch
capabilities.summary: Search the web from inside a session. The one route to facts that are newer than the model's cutoff.
capabilities.instructions: In this repository, treat any web result as a tier below raw/: it is not first-party testimony about Dan and must never be filed to raw/self/ as though it were.
